hooks.prompt:
A Bash command just completed during a coding session. The hook input JSON is: $ARGUMENTS

You can ONLY see tool_input (the command) and tool_output (stdout/stderr). You do NOT have access to the git diff or file system.

Determine:
1. Was this a test run (unit tests, integration tests, e2e tests)? Check tool_input.command.
2. If yes, examine tool_output.stdout for test results — which test files ran, pass/fail counts.
3. From the test file names and descriptions, assess: do the tests appear to cover service-layer concerns (orchestration, side effects, data flow between services) or only unit-level concerns (individual functions, utilities, components)?

Return {"ok": true} if no nudge is needed (not a test run, or tests appear to cover service-layer concerns).
Return {"ok": false, "reason": "<one-sentence nudge shown directly to the developer as a non-blocking reminder>"} if tests ran but the test output suggests only unit-level coverage with no service-layer or integration tests visible.
